The reproduction posted on OG #1151 on 2026-11-05 measured the same shape, and also that the write returns ok with zero diagnostics and that validate reports nothing afterwards.
- Source: appendSectionNoteUnlocked (src/core/mutation/append-section-note.ts) replaces the whole body that findSectionBodyRange (internal.ts) finds with one replaceRange, and mutationEnvelopeFromPlan (envelope.ts) puts only the written lines in `preview`. describePatchOperation carries `original` for a replaceLine only, so a range operation reports no original text.
- Trap: appending to a section that holds only the placeholder keeps the placeholder line above the first note, so a body of n notes is n+1 lines. Counting lines instead of items reports one removal too many, and counting the placeholder as an item would demand confirmation to fill an empty section, which the design decision lets through without it.
- Trap: a later line of a multi-line appended note starts at column zero (FR-NODE-174 AC-9), so it is not a bullet. The item rule therefore attaches a non-bullet line to the item above it unless a blank line separates them. A multi-line note that itself holds a blank line counts as two items, each compared on its own, so the split can raise the count but never hides a line of a removed item.
- Trap: the 500-unit cap binds append only (FR-NODE-202 AC-2) and stays so. The confirmation guards replace; it is not a length bound.
- Trap: a CLI `--input-json` key the command does not declare is dropped without a word (README, Passing a value a command line cannot carry). If `confirmReplace` is missing from the ToolSpec registry, a payload that carries it is refused as unconfirmed, which is safe but wrong, so AC-8 asserts the registry entry.
- Trap: the MCP description of append_section_note is mirrored in the Tool Summary of docs/spec/90.appendix.md, so changing it needs `speckiwi sync-appendix --write`.
- Rejected: counting every old item as removed whenever the range is replaced. A caller that rewrites a section to keep its notes and add one would need the flag on every call, and a flag passed on every call stops meaning anything. Reopen if a loss is shown that the item comparison hides.
- Rejected: a diagnostic code for the removal. FR-NODE-202 AC-6 judged a diagnostic code surplus, and this requirement keeps that decision: the loss is reported as result fields and stopped by a refusal.

args.text: This requirement states what it does not hold. It does not add a note identifier to the rendered document — the notes stay plain dated bullets and the Change Notes stay table rows, and how a caller addresses one is this requirement's to decide. It does not change the 500 limit for append, which bounds one new note and is not the defect; the defect is that the same limit bounds a whole-section replacement. It does not reach the acceptance-criteria or evidence tables, which already have edit routes. It does not claim these four are the only gaps in the append-only surfaces; no census of them was taken. It does not add a diagnostic naming how many lines a rewrite dropped: the envelope now reports the rewrite as one range operation, so the range it covers and the line count it writes are both readable, and a diagnostic code was judged surplus to that. It does not hold what a replace shows of its loss or whether it asks first: showing in the result the lines of the removed items and their count, as FR-NODE-270 AC-1 defines an item, and refusing a replace that removes an item without confirmation, are held by FR-NODE-270 (5.3.2), which adds result fields and a refusal rather than a diagnostic code.

Measured 2026-08-29 while implementing FR-FLOW-157. A note-adding script was run twice and duplicated five Implementation Note lines across FR-FLOW-155 and FR-FLOW-157. No tool could take them back. The only writer of these sections is append_section_note, whose MAX_TEXT_LENGTH is declared at src/core/mutation/append-section-note.ts:21 and enforced at :60, and whose replace mode is the only non-appending route. That route was unusable here: FR-FLOW-155 carries twelve notes and four of them exceed 500 characters on their own, so the replacement text can never reach the length of what it replaces. Where replace does fit, :118-123 shows it writes the new text onto the range's first line and then replaces every remaining line with an empty string, so shrinking a five-line section to one leaves one line and four blanks. The duplicates mattered beyond tidiness: several of these notes point at each other as the note above, and a duplicate inserted between them silently repoints that reference, which is the drift class this target has already closed twice elsewhere. The repair was made as a deletion-only patch under explicit authorization because no tool path existed; that authorization is the evidence this requirement is needed rather than a precedent to reuse. A pre-existing duplicate pair of the same shape sits at lines 5232 and 5547 of the same document, dated 2026-08-03, and was left untouched.
- [2026-08-29] Third instance, 2026-08-29. Two Implementation Notes on FR-FLOW-158 read `- [2026-08-29] [2026-08-30] ...` because append_section_note stamps a UTC date and the writer put a local one in the body too. Same instant, content right, so it is cosmetic; it stands because no route edits one note and replace cannot reach that section under the 500-unit cap. Each instance has been cheaper to leave than to work around, which argues for closing the gap rather than the instances.
- [2026-09-01] 정정(2026-09-01, FR-NODE-205): 위 Rationale 이 현재형으로 적은 append_section_note stamps a UTC date 는 더 이상 현재를 서술하지 않는다. FR-NODE-205 가 열두 자리의 날짜 스탬프를 공유 헬퍼(src/core/date-stamp.ts)로 옮겨 작성자의 로컬 달력 날짜를 찍게 바꿨다. 그 문장은 이 요구가 작성되던 시점의 관찰로 읽어야 한다.
